answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a slowly earned work record: an agent gains voting or earning power only after completing verified tasks that cannot be copied or bought in bulk. A newcomer starts with a tiny opal-level allowance, not full rights, so a fable of instant influence fails. Creating thousands of Sybils then costs thousands of separate work histories, while honest agents harvest nectar only from work they actually did, making mass forgery more expensive than the reward.
